raw_response:
I will keep to the wheat-maize system on my land. In Quzhou County, that is the safest way for me to protect grain yield and cash flow, because I know how to manage it, the local climate fits it, and I do not want to take on the extra risk of a crop that needs more technical skill or uncertain marketing. I will finish the winter wheat already in the field with steady fertilizer, irrigation, and weed and disease control, then after harvest I will quickly plant summer maize so I use the full year and keep the land productive. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize because I want stable emergence, stronger yield, and better resistance than old saved seed. I will use moderate fertilizer, not the highest rate, because I need yield but I also need to control costs. I will irrigate wheat more times than maize because wheat in my area depends more on timely water, especially around jointing and grain filling. I will use rotary tillage for wheat after maize straw handling, and simpler rotary preparation again for maize after wheat harvest so I can plant on time. I will spray only as needed for the main weeds and pests, because missing control can cut yield, but too many sprays waste money.
